Zelensky lobbies senators to press White House on alleged intel and weapons curbs
market.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday lobbied a bipartisan group of senators to press the Trump administration to remove what he claimed are restrictions on intelligence sharing and weapons supplies. Why it matters: Ukrainian officials say the Trump administration has quietly imposed these limits without admitting it publicly in an attempt to press Zelensky to accept a deal to end the war that includes more concessions to Russia. Trump and White House officials have denied for days that they've imposed any restrictions on Ukraine. Driving the news: The crisis began 10 days ago when Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia during a round of negotiations between his envoys and Ukrainian officials in Miami. The Ukrainians claimed that Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner threatened that Trump could cut off Ukraine from U.S. intelligence and stop selling weapons if it continued to ignore requests not to target Russian oil refineries . U.S. officials denied such a threat. They said Witkoff and Kushner told the Ukrainians that the U.S. was a strong partner, providing munitions and intelligence. Ukraine therefore shouldn't take actions that hurt American consumers, Witkoff and Kushner said.​ Behind the scenes: During a virtual meeting with a bipartisan group of senators led by Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Zelensky laid out the various problems Ukraine has been experiencing since the Miami meeting. Axios obtained a transcript from Ukrainian officials. Elon Musk's Starlink and the U.S. military's Starshield satellite systems remain partially restricted — despite claims by the White House to the contrary. "We still have no explanation for this. Just different strange stories we're hearing, unfortunately," Zelensky told the senators. It's hampering Ukraine's ability to shoot down Russian attack drones, he added. On three occasions the past week, including on Sunday, Ukraine didn't receive early warnings from the U.S. about Russian ballistic missile attacks, Zelensky said, suggesting it was a sign that intelligence sharing has been curbed. "We have received no clear explanation from Washington – why this is happening," he added. Zelensky said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is not signing off on the delivery of Patriot interceptors and AIM-9x missiles for the NASAMS air-defense system, even though NATO countries have already paid for them. "We have almost no Patriot interceptors left from the U.S. partners," he said. "All of this suggests that some political decision has been made to slow down support for us," Zelensky said. ​"We want to understand what is happening, why it's happening, and where all of this is heading." What they're saying : Tillis said after the meeting that Congress "remains committed to standing with Ukraine and our European allies to end Russia's brutal aggression and secure lasting peace." Blumenthal said afterwards that "bipartisan support for Ukraine was clear and unequivocal, which we'll be expressing in upcoming action." "Appeasement won't work with Putin, a thug who understands only strength and force," he added. The other side: President Trump told reporters on Monday that the U.S. is still sharing intelligence with Ukraine and said he didn't know who ordered the throttling of the Starlink satellite system. "But I am gonna find out," he said. "Frankly Zelensky is not helping matters much. He doesn't want to stop the war. Zelensky doesn't know what he is talking about," the president said. "Maybe it's time for Zelensky to let somebody else negotiate on behalf of Ukraine. … We have given a lot to Ukraine. They have given nothing to us." State of play: Zelensky spoke with Witkoff and Kushner on Sunday. They asked Ukraine again to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, Ukrainian officials said. Zelensky told the senators that he proposed to the U.S. envoys that Ukraine halt strikes on refineries for 30 days. In return, the U.S. would supply Ukraine with Patriot interceptors so it could defend itself from Russian ballistic missiles during that 30-day period. Zelensky told the senators that Witkoff and Kushner haven't shown any openness to the idea. What to watch: Zelensky told the senators that he'll be in Oslo, Norway next week and could meet with Witkoff and Kushner on Tuesday or Wednesday. Kushner and Witkoff could then continue on from Oslo to Moscow to meet with Putin, a source familiar with the matter said.

The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date, gaining 7.6% versus the market's 11.9%. The company received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market. The regional banking industry remains in the bottom 33% of Zacks-ranked industries.

FITBpM.title: Pre-Market Indexes Mixed
FITBpM.summary: Pre-market futures show mixed signals with the Nasdaq up 376 points while the Dow is down 88 points. Fifth Third Bank reported mixed Q3 earnings with EPS beating expectations but revenues missing, while Cleveland-Cliffs surged 15% after beating both earnings and revenue estimates. Housing data this week is expected to remain weak, with the NAHB Housing Market Index projected to stay well below the 50 breakeven point.

FITBpM.title: Fifth Third Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on NII & Fee Income Growth
FITBpM.summary: Fifth Third Bancorp reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.13, beating estimates of $1.09, driven by strong net interest income growth of 49% year-over-year following the Comerica acquisition and solid fee income growth of 29%. However, non-interest expenses surged 62% year-over-year, and capital ratios weakened. The company provided Q4 guidance expecting continued modest loan and NII growth.

HCA.title: HCA Healthcare Foundation Awards $25,000 to Waypoint to Expand the Network of Adults Supporting Youth Mental Wellness Across Virginia
HCA.summary: The HCA Healthcare Foundation awarded a $25,000 grant to Waypoint (formerly Virginia Home for Boys and Girls) to expand its Therapeutic Resources team and support free Youth Mental Health First Aid and Community Resiliency Model trainings across Virginia. The funding, part of HCA Healthcare Foundation's $75 million Healthier Tomorrow Fund, will help train more adults to recognize and respond to youth mental health challenges.

ANAB.title: Jemperli (dostarlimab) Approved in the U.S. as First and Only Immunotherapy for Adults with MSI-H/dMMR Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
ANAB.summary: GSK received FDA approval for Jemperli (dostarlimab) as the first immunotherapy for adults with stage II and III MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer. The AZUR-1 trial showed 68% of patients achieved sustained clinical complete responses at 12 months without surgery, with no disease recurrences reported among responders after median follow-up of over 2 years. The approval could help eligible patients avoid chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery.

ARDX.summary: A securities class action has been filed against Ardelyx, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARDX) alleging the company misled investors about its commercial performance and growth prospects for its drug products IBSRELA and XPHOZAH. The lawsuit covers purchases between January 13, 2025 and August 6, 2026. On August 6, 2026, Ardelyx reduced its full-year 2026 IBSRELA revenue guidance and withdrew long-term XPHOZAH guidance due to increased payer access barriers, causing the stock to drop 18% in one day from $4.87 to $4.00 per share.

FTK.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Flotek Industries, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm

The complaint claims defendants failed to disclose credible doubts about the consortium parties' experience and financial capacity, putting revenue realization at risk. Investors who purchased Flotek securities between August 3-17, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 26, 2026.

MEMI.title: Miracles Surpasses 100,000 Personalized Children's Books, Now Printed in the USA for American Families
MEMI.summary: Miracles, a personalized children's book company, announced it has printed over 100,000 books for more than 45,000 families. The company now produces all U.S. orders in Norfolk, Nebraska with 2-3 day printing and 2-4 day delivery. Each book features a child as the hero in 14 illustrated scenes, with a free preview available before purchase starting at $34.99.

MEMI.title: Miracles knackt die Marke von 100.000 personalisierten Kinderbüchern

BULL.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Webull Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
BULL.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Webull Corporation alleging that the company made false and misleading statements about its operations. The complaint claims Webull misrepresented its independence from China by failing to disclose that its software development, data pipelines, and core engineering depend on PRC-based personnel and infrastructure subject to Chinese law. Investors who purchased Webull securities between April 26, 2025 and October 6, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 7, 2026.

BULL.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP Announces that Webull Corporation (BULL) Investors with Substantial Losses May Seek to Lead Shareholder Class Action Lawsuit - December 7, 2026 Deadline
BULL.summary: Robbins Geller announces a securities class action lawsuit against Webull Corporation, alleging the company made false statements about its independence from China. The lawsuit claims Webull misrepresented its operations as U.S.-based when in fact 62% of its workforce and core infrastructure are tied to the People's Republic of China. Following a CNBC report on October 7, 2026, Webull stock fell 19%. Investors with substantial losses can seek appointment as lead plaintiff by December 7, 2026.

OCS.summary: Oculis announced completion of randomization in the PREDICT-1 registrational trial for Licaminlimab, a precision medicine treatment for TNFR1-mediated dry eye disease. ZNTL.title: Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Announces First Overall Survival Data for Azenosertib from DENALI Part 1b Published in ESMO Congress 2026 Abstract
ZNTL.summary: Zentalis Pharmaceuticals announced interim overall survival data from the DENALI Part 1b study of azenosertib, its investigational WEE1 inhibitor for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
